order.note: The entry point is NOT crafting a new container - it is the basic tier upgrade, a wooden rod and a lever, applied to a vanilla chest or barrel to convert it in place. Cheapest possible start and the thing new players miss.
The upgrade base second - iron plus planks, and it gates the entire upgrade column exactly as its sibling does in Sophisticated Backpacks.
Then tier the container up for capacity and, more importantly, upgrade slots.
The controller last - it needs a comparator and an existing wooden-tier storage block.

ladder.note: CONTAINER TIER LADDER, each crafted from the previous. Copper and iron both branch directly off the base barrel; from iron it is a single line up to netherite. The same ladder exists for chests and shulker boxes.

PARALLEL in-place upgrade items, every one of them a metal plus a LEVER. These convert a placed, full container without emptying it - the reason the mod is pleasant to use. Skip-tier variants exist too (basic straight to diamond).
Network ladder: a controller aggregates storage, links extend it to blocks that do not touch, and the io/input/output blocks give automation a defined entry and exit.
Stack upgrades climb separately. Note the difference from the backpack version: tier 1 here is built from LOGS, not a metal block, so it is far cheaper than the backpack equivalent of the same name.

gates.note: The upgrade base gates every functional upgrade, and the decoration table needs one too.
Controller, io, input and output all require an existing base-tier WOODEN storage block in the recipe - you cannot build the network out of raw materials alone.
Storage links and the storage tool need ender pearls, so the network half of the mod is Nether-gated even though the containers are not.
Shulker boxes need an actual shulker shell, so that branch is End-gated regardless of tier.

payoff.note: Upgrading a placed, full chest in-world with a lever-based tier upgrade is the standout convenience - no other storage mod in this pack does that.
Packing tape is the quiet favourite - it lets a full storage block be picked up and moved with its contents intact.
The controller turning a wall of barrels into one inventory is the structural payoff, same shape as the drawer mods.
Limited barrels are the display-friendly variant - fewer item types but much larger stacks, and they show contents on the block face.
Auto-smelting and crafting upgrades make a chest do work, which is the feature that distinguishes this from plain capacity mods.

traps.note: Infinity upgrades are creative/admin items with no survival recipe - never use as quest tasks or rewards.
Stack DOWNGRADES reduce capacity deliberately; they are filtering tools, not ladder rungs.
The debug tool and the inaccessible-slot filler are internal items that render as normal items in a naive scan. Neither belongs in a quest book.
The chipped/* upgrades duplicate the Sophisticated Backpacks ones and need Chipped blocks; they are reachable in this pack but easy to double-count across the two mods.

signature.note: Tiered containers plus in-place lever upgrades - the mod's identity is that storage improves without ever being emptied.
The decoration table and paintbrush are its other signature: storage that can be styled to match a build.
